attempted_claim: For every fixed integer d >= 3 and every fixed epsilon > 0, does there exist a deterministic algorithm running in time poly(n) which, for all sufficiently large admissible input sizes n, outputs a connected simple d-regular graph G_n on N = n(1+o(1)) vertices such that, for some constant c_d > 0, girth(G_n) >= c_d log_{d-1}(N) and max{|lambda| : lambda is a nontrivial adjacency eigenvalue of G_n} <= 2 sqrt(d-1) + epsilon, where nontrivial excludes d and, when G_n is bipartite, -d, and dN is even?
decisive_failure: No deterministic joint construction was produced and no impossibility proof was established. The blockage evidence is quantitative and local: LPS gap arithmetic, lift girth stagnation, and short-cycle first moments rule out the three concrete derandomizable routes, but do not resolve whether the target claim itself is true or false.
